license_provenance: HF dataset card YAML frontmatter `license: mit` at the pinned revision, corroborated by the card's own License section ("released under the MIT License") and by a real MIT LICENSE file in the project's code repository (github.com/AMA-Bench/AMA-Hub, "Copyright (c) 2026 AMA-Bench Team"). Not a badge. The CC-BY-4.0 that appears on arXiv:2602.22769 is arXiv's submission licence for the PAPER, shown as a CC-BY-4.0 icon on the abstract page; it does not describe the dataset. No conflict: two artifacts, two licences.

attribution.citation: Zhao et al., AMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Memory for Agentic Applications, arXiv:2602.22769, 2026

verified_shape.method: counted from the shipped JSONL at the pinned sha256; no card value trusted
defects_found: The card documents a top-level `source` field; it is absent from every one of the 208 shipped records.

TEXT2SQL: 102 trajectory turns ship `action: null` AND `observation: null` (wholly empty turns). OPENWORLD_QA: 41 turns ship an empty-string observation; TEXT2SQL a further 27. The adopted SOFTWARE slice is clean (0/3716).
The card claims the field `type` values map A/B/C/D to recall / causal inference / state updating / state abstraction; verified present and exhaustive (no other values).

label_provenance.verdict: HUMAN-AUTHORED as claimed -- adopted on the strength of an explicit, specific paper claim, with the limits of that evidence recorded below
label_provenance.evidence_quote_1: arXiv:2602.22769 S3.3.1 (wording identical in v1 and v4): "we manually annotate each selected trajectory with 12 memory-intensive QA pairs that collectively cover all categories in Tab. 2"
label_provenance.evidence_quote_2: same section: "QA pairs are then authored by graduate-level annotators with research experience in LLM agents, following shared guidelines that standardize evidence grounding and category coverage across six domains. To improve annotation reliability, each annotated trajectory undergoes a cross-review sanity check by a second annotator."
label_provenance.corroboration: The project repository (github.com/AMA-Bench/AMA-Hub, which 301-redirects to AMA-Bench/AMA-Bench) contains NO LLM-calling QA generator for the real subset. The only QA-generation code is src/synthetic_data_gen/ for TextWorld and BabyAI, and grepping it for openai|anthropic|gpt-|claude|chat.completions|llm yields only a tiktoken encoding selection and the comment "heuristic agents do not consume LLM tokens". The synthetic subset is NOT in this HF repository; the 208 shipped episodes are the real, expert-annotated subset in its entirety.
label_provenance.data_corroboration: 208 episodes x 12 QA = exactly 2496, so the stated per-trajectory quota is honored exactly; yet the A/B/C/D split is 839/596/647/414 rather than a flat 3/3/3/3, which is what human assignment under a coverage rule looks like and not what a template produces.
label_provenance.type_assignment: A/B/C/D are human-assigned as part of the same manual annotation (the guidelines standardize "category coverage"), not rule-derived.
unverified: No annotation guideline document is released, in either the repo or the HF dataset.
No annotator count is stated anywhere.

No inter-annotator agreement is reported FOR THE QA LABELS. The paper's Appendix C agreement numbers (300 instances, two annotators, majority vote, third adjudicator) belong to its judge-validation study, which is a different task -- do not read them as QA-label agreement.
No construction code ships for the real subset and no per-item provenance field exists in the JSONL, so nothing in the artifact can independently confirm or refute the authors' claim.
The paper never affirmatively rules out LLM assistance during annotation.
label_provenance.hardening_if_this_becomes_load_bearing: hand-audit ~30 swebench QA pairs against their trajectories, and ask the authors for the guideline document and annotator count.

verified_shape.paper_data_inconsistency: Paper Table 7 states 34 SWE trajectories were selected; the paper's own prose and the shipped data both say 36. Present in v1 and v4. The shipped 36 is what this lock pins.

adapter.mode: retrieval-only, $0, no reader and no judge
adapter.unit: one trajectory turn, ingested as a MemPhant episode (source_kind=agent)
adapter.probe: a SOFTWARE QA pair whose question names an explicit `step N`
adapter.gold_rule: gold unit = trajectory turn N named in the question text; deterministic regex, no model call
adapter.probe_count_note: 245 of 432 SOFTWARE questions are step-anchored (A:150, B:59, C:36, D:0). All 256 step references resolve in range (0 out-of-range). The remaining 187 need a reader and are out of scope for the $0 lane.
adapter.metric: hit@1 / hit@k on the gold turn's `unit:` tag in the recalled bodies

power.n_note: 245 step-anchored retrieval probes over 36 episodes; the full instrument is 432 QA over the same 36 episodes if a reader is funded.

resolvable_effect_size.paired_mcnemar_alpha_0.05_power_0.80: a 6.4pp absolute shift in hit@k (discordant-pair basis, assuming ~30% discordance)
resolvable_effect_size.unpaired_two_proportion_alpha_0.05_power: a ~12.5pp absolute difference between two independent arms at p~0.5
resolvable_effect_size.clustering_caveat: probes cluster in 36 episodes (median 6.8 probes/episode); the effective n for episode-level effects is 36, so treat any cross-arm claim as needing a cluster bootstrap over episodes, not a flat binomial.

retrieval_only_full_run.note: local fastembed + local Postgres; no paid call on any path

reader_ceiling_if_ever_funded.derivation: 432 QA x 8192-token budget x ~4 bytes/token = 14.2M bytes upper bound if every pack filled the budget; the 245-probe retrieval slice needs 0 paid calls. A judged full run also needs 432 judge calls. Not priced here because no provider is pinned for it.

judge_if_ever_funded.warning: AMA-Bench absolute scores are judge-dependent to the point that cross-benchmark comparison is meaningless unless the judge is pinned. The repo's own README reports Qwen3-32B (their default) is systematically lenient and worst precisely in our slice: 100 lenient cases vs 15 strict on SOFTWARE/swebench against Claude-4.6. Reported spread across judges: Qwen3-32B 0.4880, Claude-4.6 0.3986, GPT-5.4 0.3906, GPT-5.2 0.3550, DeepSeek-v3.2 0.3309. Their own recommendation is Claude-4.6 as reference judge or ensemble voting.
judge_if_ever_funded.official_judge_prompt: utils/evaluation_metrics.py::judge_prompt -- binary yes/no over (question, reference answer, predicted answer)
